title: Decode String
description:
Given an encoded string `s`, return its decoded string.

The encoding rule is: `k[encoded_string]`, where the `encoded_string` inside the square brackets is repeated exactly `k` times. Note that `k` is guaranteed to be a positive integer.

You may assume that the input string is always valid: there are no extra white spaces, square brackets are well-formed, and encoded substrings may be nested arbitrarily deeply. Furthermore, the original data does not contain any digits — digits are only used for the repeat numbers `k` (for example, inputs like `3a` or `2[4]` will not occur).

Test cases are generated so that the length of the decoded output will never exceed `10^5`.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters, digits, and square brackets '[' and ']'.
s is guaranteed to be a valid encoded string.
All repeat counts k are integers in the range [1, 300].
The length of the decoded output will not exceed 10^5.
hints: Because encoded blocks can be nested inside other encoded blocks, think about saving your current string prefix and repeat count whenever you enter '['.
Maintain a stack of (previous_string, repeat_count) pairs (or two parallel stacks). Remember that repeat counts k can have multiple digits.
When you see ']', pop the saved prefix and repeat count, repeat the current string k times, and append it to the saved prefix.

examples.explanation: "a" is repeated 3 times and "bc" is repeated 2 times, producing "aaabcbc".
The inner "2[c]" decodes to "cc", so "a2[c]" becomes "acc", repeated 3 times to give "accaccacc".
